title: The Enforcement Gap
excerpt: Europe has the most advanced digital-safety framework in the world on paper. Eighteen months into active enforcement, the DSA's entire fine record is two decisions — while the tools built to fix that sit unused in the statute book.

title: The Blind Spot in Europe's Child Safety Law
excerpt: Article 34(1)(b) of the Digital Services Act names non-discrimination and children's rights in the same clause — but the Commission's Article 28 guidelines on protecting minors operate through identity-neutral categories, with no requirement to disaggregate harm by protected characteristic.

title: The Fine That Missed the Point
excerpt: The EU's €120 million fine against X addressed advertising transparency. The far more consequential violation — a documented, billion-view amplification pattern — has not been charged under Articles 34–35 of the DSA. Here's the legal case for why it should be.

title: The Law That Punishes the Women It Claims to Protect
excerpt: France's face-covering ban was written for perhaps 1,900 women. A decade of enforcement data across ten European countries shows who these laws actually punish — and it isn't who the justification claims.

title: When the Law Exists but Cannot Be Reached
excerpt: Nearly one in two Muslims in the EU has experienced racial discrimination. Only 6% ever file a complaint. The problem isn't an absence of law — it's an absence of access to it.

title: The Name Penalty in Europe
excerpt: Across Europe, a name is often enough to decide whether a CV gets a callback, an application gets a reply, or a family gets flagged for fraud. The evidence for it is no longer anecdotal — it's documented, and in places, government-funded.

title: Anti-Muslim Discrimination in Europe: A Documented Record
excerpt: Primary FRA survey data, named and sourced incidents of state action against religious practice, the legal reasoning for where these measures fail proportionality, and platform X's documented role in amplifying anti-Muslim narratives to over a billion views.

title: Formal DSA Complaint Against X Corp — Articles 34–35
excerpt: The formal complaint filed with the European Commission arguing that X's documented pattern of anti-Muslim content amplification constitutes a failure to meet its systemic-risk obligations under Articles 34–35 of the Digital Services Act.

title: Formal Submission: Closing the Minors' Discrimination Blind Spot in DSA Guidelines
excerpt: The formal submission to DG CONNECT requesting that the Commission's Article 28 guidelines on protecting minors be revised to require platforms to disaggregate harm data by protected characteristic — the regulatory ask behind The Blind Spot in Europe's Child Safety Law.

title: Legal Memorandum: DSA Enforcement Architecture for Minors' Rights
excerpt: The full legal analysis behind the X Corp. complaint and the minors' discrimination submission — an article-by-article DSA enforcement memorandum. Available for licensing; not published in full.
